capitals.name: Topoxte (Yaxha lagoon)
capitals.note: The page names Topoxte on the Yaxha lagoon, which it says was abandoned before 1697; Yaxha's coordinates stand in and the Kowoj seat (Zacpeten on Lake Salpeten) is not on the page.

Confidence 2 (reviewer am-02): the Kowoj page dates the conquest to 1697 but names no conqueror, and says Topoxte was abandoned before it (main towns Zacpeten and Ixlu).

sources.title: Kowoj
sources.note: Late Postclassic (ca. 1250-1697); migrated from Mayapan after 1441; Topoxte on the Yaxha lagoon abandoned before the conquest of 1697.

sources.title: Yaxha
sources.note: Read for the coordinates of Yaxha (17°4′39″N 89°24′9″W) used to place the Yaxha lagoon.

notes: NEW STATE, THIN. Cliopatria has no Kowoj row; the Petén lakes lie inside Later Mayan City-States from 1450. The page is short: it has no dated wars with the Itza, no extent and no capital date. 1441 is the Mayapan collapse after which the Kowoj 'claimed to have migrated'; the 1250 in the opening sentence is a period range. The Itza dossier (itza-mayans) names the Kowoj as the hostile eastern lakes. Kejache (40 by 100 km, Cortés 1525, encomienda 1543, 'Tzuktok' frontier) and Yalain, Manche Ch'ol and Lakandon Ch'ol have no dossier here: the Kejache page gives an area but no centre.
